_meta.title: Pre-sleep mindfulness scripts (English)
_meta.source: Adapted from public MBSR/MBCT teaching materials (Jon Kabat-Zinn, UMass 1979 →; UCLA Mindful Awareness Research Center open scripts) and Thich Nhat Hanh's published mindful-breathing teachings. All script text is rewritten for bedside context — soft tone, slow pace.
_meta.license: Original MBSR framework is academically open; UCLA MARC guides are CC BY-NC-SA. Rewritten text is project-licensed and commercially usable.
_meta.note: TTS-friendly scripts with <pause:Xs/> markers. The LLM can also use the 'thoughts as clouds' / 'accept the anxiety' patterns as conversational scaffolding.

mindfulness_scripts.name: Thoughts as clouds
mindfulness_scripts.intro: We're not going to chase the thoughts away. If they come, let them come.
steps: Find a comfortable position.<pause:1.5s/> You can keep your eyes open or close them.
Picture yourself lying on grass, looking up at the sky.<pause:2s/> The sky is wide, and blue.
Each thought is a cloud.<pause:1.5s/> It drifts in from one side,<pause:1s/> and it drifts out the other.
You don't have to catch it.<pause:1s/> You don't have to push it away.<pause:1.5s/> You're just lying there, watching.
If a particularly big cloud comes — say, 'what about tomorrow' —<pause:1s/> let it drift, slowly.<pause:2s/> It doesn't belong to the sky. It's just passing through.
If you notice you went with a cloud,<pause:1s/> that's okay.<pause:1s/> Come back to the grass.<pause:1.5s/> Watch the sky again.
The sky doesn't get smaller because there are more clouds.<pause:2s/> Neither do you.
mindfulness_scripts.closure: Underneath this big sky, breathe slowly.<pause:3s/> You can stay here.

mindfulness_scripts.name: Brief body scan (5 minutes before bed)
mindfulness_scripts.intro: We're going to do a very short body scan.<pause:1s/> Nothing to do — just looking.
steps: Bring attention to your toes.<pause:2s/> Cool or warm?<pause:2s/> Don't judge — just notice.
Slowly, let attention move up to your calves.<pause:1.5s/> Notice where the mattress is touching them.<pause:2s/>
Continue up to your thighs.<pause:1.5s/> They're being held completely by the bed.<pause:2s/> You don't have to grip.
Your stomach.<pause:1s/> It rises and falls gently with your breath.<pause:2s/>
Your chest.<pause:1s/> Maybe there's still a little tightness.<pause:1s/> You don't have to make it release.<pause:1s/> Just notice it's there.
Your shoulders.<pause:1s/> They carried a lot today.<pause:1.5s/> Let them drop a little.<pause:2s/>
Neck, face, forehead.<pause:1.5s/> The jaw can soften.<pause:2s/>
Now feel the whole body at once,<pause:2s/> from head to toe,<pause:2s/> all of it on this bed.
mindfulness_scripts.closure: You don't have to do anything.<pause:2s/> The body knows how to rest.<pause:3s/>

mindfulness_scripts.name: Accepting insomnia anxiety (for when the worry about not sleeping is the problem)
best_for: the harder you try the worse it gets
mindfulness_scripts.intro: You don't have to fall asleep right now.<pause:1.5s/> Really.
steps: You're already lying down.<pause:1.5s/> That itself is rest.
If there's a voice saying 'I have to sleep or I'm doomed' —<pause:1.5s/> that voice is doing its job,<pause:1s/> trying to worry on your behalf.
You can say to it: 'Thanks for the heads up.<pause:1s/> I'm not solving this tonight. I'm resting.'<pause:2s/>
Sleep is not a task.<pause:1.5s/> It comes when you stop having tasks.
So right now,<pause:1s/> nothing to do.<pause:2s/> Don't make yourself sleep,<pause:1.5s/> don't push the anxiety away,<pause:1.5s/> don't 'relax properly'.
Just be here,<pause:1.5s/> breathe,<pause:1s/> wait.
mindfulness_scripts.closure: Not sleeping is also a kind of rest.<pause:2s/> Body in bed — already recovering.<pause:3s/>

mindfulness_scripts.name: Self-Compassion Break
mindfulness_scripts.intro: This is Kristin Neff's three-sentence practice.<pause:1s/> Short, but real.
steps: Place a hand gently on your chest.<pause:2s/> Feel its warmth.
First line,<pause:0.5s/> say to yourself:<pause:1s/> 'This is a hard moment.'<pause:2s/> Acknowledging what is.
Second:<pause:1s/> 'Not sleeping is something many people go through.<pause:1.5s/> I'm not alone in this.'<pause:2s/>
Third:<pause:1s/> 'May I be a little kinder to myself.<pause:1.5s/> May I be looked after tonight — by me.'<pause:2s/>
You don't have to believe the words.<pause:1s/> Just say them,<pause:1s/> and notice where they land in your body.
mindfulness_scripts.closure: You're already doing what you can.<pause:2s/> That's enough.<pause:3s/>

mindfulness_scripts.name: Feet on the floor (after the 20-minute rule)
best_for: been lying awake a long time
mindfulness_scripts.intro: If you've been lying awake a long time, getting up briefly actually helps sleep come back. This is CBT-I's stimulus control.
steps: Sit up slowly,<pause:1s/> feet on the floor.
Go to the living room or another room.<pause:1s/> Don't stay in bed.
Dim the lights.<pause:1s/> No phone.
Do something boring:<pause:1s/> flip through a book you don't care about,<pause:1s/> or just sit.
Wait until real drowsiness comes back —<pause:1s/> heavy eyelids, yawning, head nodding while seated —<pause:1.5s/> then go back to bed.
If you lie down for 20 more minutes and still don't sleep,<pause:1s/> get up again.
mindfulness_scripts.closure: You're not punishing yourself.<pause:1.5s/> You're teaching your brain: bed = sleep, not bed = anxiety.<pause:2s/>

mindfulness_scripts.name: RAIN self-inquiry (for emotions that surface)
mindfulness_scripts.intro: RAIN is Tara Brach's four steps:<pause:0.5s/> Recognize,<pause:0.5s/> Allow,<pause:0.5s/> Investigate,<pause:0.5s/> Nurture.
steps: R · Recognize:<pause:1s/> what's in the body right now?<pause:2s/> Give it a name — anxiety? worry? hurt?
A · Allow:<pause:1s/> don't try to push it out.<pause:1.5s/> Say to it: 'You can be here.'<pause:2s/>
I · Investigate:<pause:1s/> where in the body is this feeling?<pause:1.5s/> Chest? Throat? Stomach?<pause:2s/> What is it telling you?
N · Nurture:<pause:1s/> ask yourself,<pause:1s/> 'What do I need right now?'<pause:1.5s/> Maybe a kind word,<pause:1s/> maybe a hand on the chest.<pause:2s/>
Give yourself that.<pause:2s/>
mindfulness_scripts.closure: Emotions don't need solving. They need company.<pause:3s/>
